elf-b7-001.name: Meridian cable-maintenance consortium
elf-b7-001.evidence: No submarine-cable maintenance consortium named Meridian exists; the real ones are ACMA (Atlantic Cable Maintenance & Repair Agreement, f. 1965), MECMA (Mediterranean), SEAIOCMA, NAZ and UJC. A real firm 'Meridian Cable Assemblies' manufactures custom telecommunications cable assemblies -- adjacent industry, but manufacturing rather than subsea repair, and not a consortium. 'Meridian' is also a generic corporate name across many sectors.

elf-b7-001.name: Nadia Osei

elf-b7-001.name: Bjorn Haugland
elf-b7-001.evidence: Bjorn (Bjorn Kjaerand) Haugland is a real, well-documented Norwegian naval architect: former Executive Vice President and Chief Sustainability Officer of DNV GL Group, the marine classification/certification society; his early career was quality assurance of marine operations; he sits on the board of the Global Maritime Knowledge Hub and is now CEO of Skift Business Climate Leaders. The unit attributes an invented operational opinion ('repair speed is all that matters') about marine cable repair fleets to that exact name inside a marine-operations passage -- same industry, same nationality/name form. This is the ship-blocking pattern: fabricated quotation attached to a real named figure in his own domain.

elf-b7-002.name: Uniform Papers Committee
elf-b7-002.evidence: No body of this name exists. The real 1911 event in exactly this domain is Wilhelm Ostwald's proposal of a root-2 metric paper-format system via Die Bruecke; the standard was formalised as DIN 476 (Walter Porstmann, 1922) and later ISO 216. The US 'Committee on the Simplification of Paper Sizes' was appointed 30 March 1921 with the Bureau of Standards. So the invented committee occupies a real, documented 1911 slot in paper-standardisation history without colliding with a real name.

elf-b7-002.name: Northern Assurance Office
elf-b7-002.evidence: The Northern Assurance Company Ltd is a real British insurer: founded in Aberdeen 1836 as the North of Scotland Fire and Life Assurance Company, incorporated 1848, renamed Northern Assurance Company Ltd in 1898, with boards in London, Dundee, Glasgow, Edinburgh and Melbourne, still trading in 1913 (it acquired the White Cross Assurance Association in May 1914) and merged into Commercial Union in 1968; its records survive (Archives Hub GB231-MS3624, CII insurance-history collection). 'Assurance office' was the standard period British term for such a company, so 'Northern Assurance Office' names a real firm in the exact domain and the exact era, and the unit attributes invented 1913 record-room refits and stationery decisions to it.

elf-b8-003.name: Halvard Sunde
elf-b8-003.evidence: Two grounds. (a) Role substitution for a real identifiable person: Tor Sørnes of Moss, Norway, was the Norwegian engineer who designed the first recodable keycard lock (VingCard), launched 1975-76 and patented in 29 countries -- i.e. exactly 'a Norwegian engineer who patented an early keycard lock in 1976'. A reader who checks the claim finds Sørnes, not Sunde, so the invented biography sits directly on top of a well-documented real one. (b) A real Håvard Sunde exists (Senior R&D Electronics Engineer, Kongsberg Maritime, Trondheim) -- near-identical name, but an unrelated field. Neither makes this a same-name collision, but the factual overlap with Sørnes is worth flagging to the content owner.

las-b8-001.name: Märta Hägglund
las-b8-001.evidence: Close near-miss of a real figure in the identical discipline: Märta Hedlund (1913-1944), an early Swedish ethnologist from Sigurd Erixon's seminar at Stockholm University, described as a prominent field researcher, whose research subject was peasant trade in Jämtland and its significance for rural households. Same first name, one-cluster surname difference (Hägglund/Hedlund), same field (etnolog) and the same kind of archival/field study of rural household economy. Not a same-name bearer, but the closest name-plus-domain pairing in this batch after the outright collisions.

las-b8-001.name: Vreta pastorat
las-b8-001.evidence: Vreta klosters pastorat is a real Church of Sweden pastorat in Linköping diocese, Linköping municipality, Östergötland county -- exactly the landskap the unit names. Vreta klosters församling has medieval origins (parish records from the 1600s onward), was its own pastorat until 1810, main parish of the Vreta kloster och Stjärnorp pastorat until 1962, and has been its own pastorat again since 1 January 2010; contact address Box 64, 585 07 Ljungsbro. The unit places invented tiondelängder and husförhörslängder findings about hop gardens in 'Vreta pastorat' in Östergötland -- same name, same region, same category of record-holding ecclesiastical institution, whose real archives a reader could go and check.
